name: HyperFrames
tagline: A video maker for AI: describe what you want, and out comes a polished MP4 - no camera, no editing app.
sentence: Ask Claude Code to make a product demo or a recap video: HyperFrames turns a web page into an animated MP4, complete with titles, charts and transitions.
replaces: Canva video, Loom or a freelance editor for short product demos and recap clips

visual.alt: A HyperFrames video template called 'Biennale Yellow': large navy serif type reading 'Paper, ink & yellow' on a warm parchment background with a soft yellow glow, with metadata showing Register: Literary-editorial, Ground: Warm parchment, Type: Instrument Serif and Archivo, Depth: Atmospheric blooms.
visual.caption: One of 20+ built-in design templates. You pick a look, give it your content, and HyperFrames renders the video.

board.say: You need a short product video or a recap clip, but you don't have a camera, a video editor, or the time to learn one.
board.eg: A one-minute demo of your new feature: right now, that means a screen recorder, a video editor, and an afternoon.

board.say: You ask Claude Code (or any coding agent) to make the video, or type a command yourself.
board.eg: `/hyperframes 'Make a 30-second product demo for our new dashboard'` - the agent writes the page and renders the video.

board.say: A description of what you want, or a web page with timing marks that say when each part appears.
board.eg: A product name, a few bullet points, and a design template like 'Biennale Yellow' or 'Bold Poster.'

board.say: It builds each frame from your content and renders them into a video file.
steps: The agent writes a web page with your content, picks a template and adds animation timing
HyperFrames opens each frame in a browser engine (the same tool web browsers use to draw pages), captures it as a picture, and stitches the pictures into a video
It mixes in audio, captions or transitions if you asked for them, and writes the final MP4 file
board.eg: The README's own example: one command renders an MP4 from an HTML template, deterministically - the same input always produces the same video.

board.say: A finished MP4 video, ready to share or post.

outputs.eg: A 30-second MP4 you can post to LinkedIn, attach to a Slack message, or embed in a slide deck
20+ built-in design themes (editorial, poster, capsule, grid) you can swap for a different look without redoing the content
Change one number in the content and re-render: the video updates in seconds, not hours

before: Making a short product video means a screen recorder, a video editor, and half a day of cutting and arranging.
Updating a video after a product change means redoing the whole process from scratch.
after: Describe what you want and get a rendered MP4 in seconds - no camera, no editor, no editing skills.
Change the content and re-render: the video updates automatically, like re-printing a document.
uses_note: HyperFrames is 7 months old with over 4 million installs on skills.sh. Real named uses from outside the maker's own team are still hard to find in public - most adoption is through Claude Code agents where the output (a video) is what gets shared, not the tool that made it.

steps: [Install the HyperFrames plugin](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) in Claude Code: type `claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes` and wait for it to finish.
Ask Claude Code to make a video: try `Make a 30-second product overview video for a fictional coffee delivery app called BeanDrop, using the Biennale Yellow template.`
Play the MP4 file it creates. Change one detail in the content and ask [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) to re-render - the updated video arrives in seconds.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes

If that scan passes: install the plugin, make a 30-second demo video using one of the built-in templates, and show me the result. Then change one line of content and re-render. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: About **240 MB** for development (includes test files via Git LFS). The plugin install itself is lighter.
footprint.memory: No data found for a specific number. Rendering uses a browser engine to capture frames, so memory depends on the complexity of the page.
footprint.runs_on: Mac, Windows, Linux. Needs Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg (a free video-encoding tool, installed automatically on most systems).

best_for: You need short product demos, recap clips or social videos and don't have a video editor or the time to learn one
You already use Claude Code and want to make videos by describing them, not by dragging clips on a timeline
skip_if: You need to film real people or real places - HyperFrames renders designed pages, not camera footage
You want a drag-and-drop video editor with a visual timeline - this is a code-to-video tool, not a traditional editor

alternatives.name: Canva Video
alternatives.line: A drag-and-drop video maker with templates - easier to start with, but you can't automate it from a coding agent or re-render by changing one line.

alternatives.name: Remotion
alternatives.line: An open-source code-to-video tool that uses React (a web-development framework). More flexible for developers, but harder to start with if you're not writing code yourself.

watch: **Made by HeyGen, an AI video company.** HyperFrames is their open-source project (Apache 2.0 license), not a community effort. HeyGen's paid products are separate.
**It renders designed pages, not camera footage.** If you need to film a person talking, this isn't the tool. It's for animated graphics, charts, titles and transitions.
**Needs FFmpeg installed.** FFmpeg is a free video tool that most systems have or can install automatically, but if it's missing, the render step will fail with an error.
